clue.text: Poetic work the first with dramatic stakes? Guess not...

indicators.note: the first of the following word means only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: opening letter of the word
antes are the stakes put in before a hand of poker
to infer is to deduce or guess
a simple negative

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a famous poem was the first to feature theatrical stakes, then decides against it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is DANTE'S INFERNO, the poem the whole puzzle is themed on; 'stakes' looks like wooden posts but means gambling antes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Inferno is the first part of the Divine Comedy, a long narrative poem from medieval Italy.

clue.text: One taken in by proof all made up

definitions.text: One taken in by proof all made up

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it
made up means invented or concocted, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is duped by evidence that was entirely fabricated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the wordplay builds APRIL FOOL, and the full sentence describes one, a person taken in by a made-up story.
explanation.definitionFit: An April fool is the victim of a hoax played on the first of April, someone deceived by an invented tale.

clue.text: Caught on top of tower with specially picked locks

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of the word
wearing a wig, that is having hair chosen and put on specially

explanation.surface: A captive is grabbed atop a tower whose locks have been carefully picked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door locks being picked by a burglar, but it means hair, here a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Twigged is British slang for understood or realised, the same idiom as caught on.

clue.text: Second husband a big hit – or old hat

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for second
the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
a knockout, the biggest punch in boxing

explanation.surface: A woman's second husband is either a smash hit or a has-been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' reads as the idiom for dated, but here it is literal: a military hat of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume, worn by soldiers in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Church centres called out scoundrels

indicators.note: called out means spoken, so we want a word pronounced like the one indicated

blocks.note: knaves are rogues, and the K is silent

explanation.surface: Villains get denounced from the heart of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The nave is the central main body of a church building where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Body part some heard rumbling

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters, taken in a run

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A few people heard a rumbling noise from somewhere inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound, a part of human anatomy.

clue.text: Futile gesture snubbed by crossword setters online

indicators.note: snubbed is read as cut short, like a snub nose, so the word loses its tail

blocks.note: a nod of the head is a gesture
setters refer to themselves as me or us
E as in email or e-commerce

explanation.surface: A puzzle compiler's pointless gesture is ignored by fellow setters on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: NOD loses its last letter; the plural 'setters' gives US rather than the usual ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futile has no purpose or result, which is the plain meaning of the phrase no use.

clue.text: Detective to probe corrupt Vatican ruler's principles

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are disordered
to probe something is to go into it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Detective Inspector, a British police rank

explanation.surface: A detective investigates a corrupt pope's moral principles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vatican setting suggests cardinals in the surface, which helps the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The cardinal virtues are prudence, justice, temperance and fortitude, the four key moral principles in classical and Christian thought.

clue.text: Reminder to include right solution

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder, as given to an actor
the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A prompt nudges someone toward the correct answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solution' looks like a crossword answer but means a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure is a remedy that resolves an illness, just as a solution resolves a problem.

clue.text: A couple of significant others nothing to write home about

blocks.note: SO is the abbreviation for significant other, and a couple means two of them

explanation.surface: A pair of partners turn out to be thoroughly unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre or merely average, the same idea as the idiom for something unremarkable.

clue.text: What holy folk will give in Frankie and Benny's, maybe?

definitions.text: What holy folk will give in Frankie and Benny's, maybe?

blocks.clueFragment: What holy folk will give in Frankie and Benny's, maybe?
blocks.note: surface reading: what devout diners would ask for at a high-street restaurant
setter's reading: the requests pious people place with a waiter, and also the name for communities of monks and nuns

explanation.surface: Pious customers placing their requests at a chain restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Frankie and Benny's is a British chain of Italian-American restaurants; what religious diners give there are their orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious orders are communities such as Benedictines or Franciscans, and the phrase also literally means meal requests made by devout people.

clue.text: Latin poet's moving verse for abyss

indicators.note: moving the verse abbreviation means shifting that one letter to a new place in the name

blocks.note: Ovid, the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses

explanation.surface: A Roman poet's stirring lines describe a bottomless pit.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the abbreviation for verse; moving it from second place to first turns OVID into VOID.
explanation.definitionFit: A void is an empty space or chasm, which is what an abyss is.

clue.text: Location down under home to certain devils reclining on throne?

definitions.note: a past tense verb defined by a description of the state

indicators.note: something reclining lies back, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.clueFragment: Location down under home to certain devils
blocks.note: Tasmania, the Australian state where Tasmanian devils live, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Devils lounging on a throne in their Australian home.
explanation.walkthrough: Tasmanian devils are marsupials native to the island state of Tasmania; Tas is its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who sat was seated, as one is when installed on a throne; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: NASA program regularly blocked sites

indicators.note: with every other letter blocked out, only the ones at regular intervals remain

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A NASA programme kept getting barred from websites.
explanation.definitionFit: STS stands for Space Transportation System, the official name of the space shuttle programme run by NASA.

clue.text: Successfully sunbathe in vessel with bottom out

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the final letter, and out means it is dropped

blocks.note: a tank is a container for liquid

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sunbathe in a tub with no base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan is to brown the skin in sunlight, the result a sunbather hopes to achieve.

clue.text: Mephistopheles initially leading wicked staff

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the name is used
leading means going in front of the next piece

blocks.note: the opening letter of the devil's name
in slang both wicked and ace mean excellent

explanation.surface: The devil Mephistopheles heads a wicked team of employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' and 'staff' both read as evil workers; they mean slang approval and a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy ceremonial or fighting club, a kind of staff carried as a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Firm friend swallows pill before large red

indicators.note: something that swallows another takes it inside
before means placed ahead of what follows

blocks.note: short for company
rhyming slang: china plate means mate
an ecstasy tablet
the clothing-size abbreviation

explanation.surface: A loyal friend takes a tablet before a large glass of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), and E is drug slang for an ecstasy pill.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson dye made from crushed insects, used to colour food red.

clue.text: Accused person may enter this place with endless heat

indicators.note: with no ends means both the first and last letters of the word go

blocks.note: the abbreviation for place, as in street names
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A defendant walks into somewhere unbearably hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter' looks like going into a place, but one enters a plea in court; 'endless' trims both ends of heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A defendant enters a plea of guilty or not guilty when formally answering a charge in court.

clue.text: Insiders from navy like a certain Bond dealing with gadgets in the air

definitions.text: dealing with gadgets in the air

indicators.note: the insiders of a word are its middle letters, without the outer ones

blocks.note: the two inner letters
an ionic bond is a type of chemical bond

explanation.surface: Naval insiders resemble a famous spy who handles gadgets while flying.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B suggests James Bond and his gadgets, but this is the chemistry bond.
explanation.definitionFit: Avionic relates to avionics, the electronic equipment and systems used in aircraft.

clue.text: Casino's hosting 21, perhaps

indicators.note: a word hosting something holds it within its own letters

blocks.note: the letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A gambling house offers the card game twenty-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 looks like blackjack in a casino, but it is the cross-reference to 21-down, envy, one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is one of the seven deadly sins, so the answer to 21 is an example of a sin.

clue.text: Fire and brimstone beginning to affect label on pants

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: brimstone is sulphur, chemical symbol S
the opening letter
Calvin Klein, the brand name on the waistband of underpants

explanation.surface: A hellfire preacher's message starts to change the logo on underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire and brimstone' reads as one phrase, but 'Fire' is the definition, as in dismiss; pants are underpants in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack someone is to dismiss them from a job, which is what fire means here.

clue.text: Rejecting "siestas", I don't say a word in this language

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: siestas are afternoon naps
taken as written
the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone refusing a nap stays silent, hinting at the language the word siesta comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: Siesta is itself a Spanish word, which ties the surface to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish is the language from which the word siesta was borrowed, so it is the language referred to.

clue.text: The first day of advent's flipping cold

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: December 1, the date Advent calendars begin

explanation.surface: It is bitterly cold on the first day of Advent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive qualifying cold, but it reverses the date.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means frozen or chilled, so something iced is cold.

clue.text: What sounds just like its heart's desire

indicators.note: sounds just like means the word is pronounced exactly as the letters named after it

blocks.note: the heart of the four-letter answer is its middle pair of letters, N and V, said by their names

explanation.surface: A riddle about something that echoes exactly what the heart longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue refers to itself: the middle two letters of the answer, N and V, spoken aloud give the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is resentful longing for what someone else has, a covetous kind of desire.

clue.text: Fiendish act I'm in on with liar is creating offence

indicators.note: fiendish means devilishly cruel or complicated, so the letters are tangled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wicked scheme shared with a liar ends up causing offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offence' reads as hurt feelings but means a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminalisation is the act of making something illegal, that is turning it into a new crime in law.

clue.text: Newspaper carrying Methuselah's second-rate bits of verse

indicators.note: in a down clue the paper below carries the other pieces on top of it

blocks.note: the setter Methuselah is speaking, so Methuselah is means I am
B grade is second class
the i is a British daily newspaper

explanation.surface: A paper prints the setter's mediocre fragments of poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is this puzzle's setter, so his 's stands for is and he is I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi are iambs, metrical feet of a short syllable then a long one, the building blocks of a line of poetry.

clue.text: One who's six feet under concerned with cave

blocks.note: an insect has six legs, and many live underground
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone dead and buried is linked to a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six feet under' is the idiom for dead and buried, but here it is a six-legged creature living below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Antre is a poetic word for a cave or cavern, used by Shakespeare in Othello.

clue.text: Amigo spoiled how The Metamorphosis ends

indicators.note: spoiled means damaged or messed up, so the letters are put in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend ruined the ending of Kafka's famous story.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals point to Kafka's novella, but the metamorphosis meant is an insect's.
explanation.definitionFit: The imago is the final adult form of an insect, the stage at which its metamorphosis is complete.

clue.text: Obviously diabolical spirit's vile and tart when drunk by yard

indicators.note: being drunk leaves things confused and staggering, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a demon is an evil spirit, with the possessive S
taken as written
taken as written
the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: An evil spirit is plainly nasty and sour after a drinking session in the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Demonstratively means in a way that openly shows or makes plain, close to obviously or evidently.

clue.text: Underground Zones 1-9 – might four answers here be called one of them?

blocks.note: surface reading: the fare zones of the London Underground; setter's reading: the nine levels of the underworld in Dante

blocks.clueFragment: might four answers here be called one of them?
blocks.note: the four three-letter answers in the centre of the grid ring a black square, and reading round them spells the name of the devil found in the innermost level

explanation.surface: A question about London Tube fare zones and whether four grid answers belong to one.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT, STS, TAN and SIN encircle the centre, and SAT running into TAN reads SATAN, whom Dante places at the bottom of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's Inferno divides hell into nine concentric circles, numbered one to nine as one descends underground.
